title: Incremental token-signal telemetry and adaptive redaction for hybrid streaming/tool-invocation
creator: Ava Park
description:
Goal: Ship a production-safe telemetry and redaction approach for streamed responses that interleave tool/function calls and structured outputs. We want per-token/per-chunk signal metrics and trace spans that make it easy to diagnose partial outputs and tool boundaries while ensuring logs and observability streams do not leak PII. This ticket scopes an implementation that emits incremental token-signal metrics, correlates per-chunk tracing spans with tool invocation events, and performs context-aware redaction in the streaming path without materially increasing tail latency.

Background: Current streaming observability emits chunk-level counters but lacks token-quality signals (e.g., hallucination score, stop-token proximity, tool-boundary confidence) and robust per-chunk PII redaction. Tool calls interleaved in the stream complicate trace stitching and raise the risk of emitting sensitive payloads before redaction policies apply.

Non-goals: Full content-aware DLP classification for all customer data (out of scope), and changing the core streaming protocol. We will implement as-compatible-with existing streaming API and provide a flag to enable conservative "safe-mode" redaction for enterprise tenants.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Emit incremental telemetry for each stream chunk that includes: chunk_id, token_count, delta_tokens, per-token signal buckets (as histogram name), tool_boundary boolean, span_id correlator.
- Tracing: a span is started on stream open, child spans on each tool/function call, and a per-chunk lightweight span enriched with the correlator header. Spans must be linkable from Console (trace view) to logs and dashboards.
- Redaction: Implement a two-stage redaction pipeline: fast deterministic scrub (regex/token blocklist) applied synchronously before emission; asynchronous contextual scrub (NLP-based) that can redact late and trigger a retract event (stream-fallback) if necessary.
- No PII should appear in logs/metrics exported to external SaaS telemetry backends when tenant has "enterprise.safe-mode" enabled.
- Measure latency regression: p50/p95 end-to-end token latency increase <= 5ms / 20ms respectively on our baseline load for a standard gpt-like 8k request.
- Feature flag and per-tenant controls in Console for sampling rates and safe-mode behavior.

Design notes and tradeoffs: 
- Deterministic scrub (regex/blocklist) is cheap and prevents most accidental leaks; however it has false positives and negatives. We therefore add an async contextual scrub to cover complex patterns, but it can only redact retrospectively: for that we implement a "retract" message (application-level control) that signals the client to drop or replace previously emitted content. Retract messages are rate-limited and gated behind enterprise contracts.
- To avoid emitting sensitive fields in telemetry, token-signals are aggregated into named buckets (e.g., "safety_risk:[0-3]") rather than streaming raw tokens. This retains diagnostic value while reducing surface area.
- Tracing uses lightweight per-chunk spans with sampling by default (1%) and deterministic sampling for tool-calls and error paths. This reduces cost while preserving developer debuggability.
- We will not attempt full PII redaction inside model internals; instead we rely on fast filters + retract semantics + tenant opt-in for aggressive contextual redaction.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Wire new telemetry schema into serving runtime's streaming emitter: add chunk metadata fields (chunk_id, span_link, token_signal_buckets).
2) Implement deterministic scrub module in runtime output path (C++/Rust), apply before chunk flush. Provide config for blocklist and regex rules per-tenant.
3) Hook tracing: start parent span on request accept, create child spans for tool_call start/end, attach chunk span IDs as tags. Ensure Console can join spans by correlator.
4) Async contextual redaction service: lightweight microservice that receives queued candidate strings and returns redact masks; when it returns a redact that affects emitted content, runtime emits a retract delta and an audit event.
5) Safe-mode: when enabled, synchronous scrub is stricter (extra blocklist), contextual redact runs at higher priority and certain chunk emissions are withheld until scrub verdict when feasible.
6) Expose flags and sampling controls in Console + API for tenancy.

Telemetry schema example (informational):
chunk_event = {
  "chunk_id": "uuid",
  "seq_offset": 0,
  "tokens_emitted": 12,
  "token_signal_buckets": ["safety_risk:0","stop_prob:low"],
  "tool_boundary": "none|tool-xyz",
  "span_link": "trace-id:span-id"
}

Monitoring & metrics: track: per-chunk emission rate, retract rate, contextual-redact-latency, p50/p95 token latency delta, sensitive-content-detection-rate. Buckets should be numeric histograms in Console.

Rollout plan: feature-flag gated rollout staged by tenant: internal -> beta customers -> opt-in enterprises -> default. Start with sampling enabled and conservative scrub rules, then relax or tighten by customer feedback.

Security: Security review required (see security_review_required). We will produce a formal threat model doc and run SAST on the contextual-redact service.

2026-03-05 - Prototype implemented: deterministic scrub in runtime + chunk_id emission. Initial internal perf: +1.8ms p50, +7ms p95. Logged sample PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/9872
2026-03-08 - UX: Console team requested an additional 'retract' visualization and a per-tenant safe-mode toggle. Created UX ticket PM-814.

2026-03-10 - Observability: initial metrics surfaced in staging dashboards. Retract events are visible as 'stream.retract' with tenant tag. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/stream-retracts
2026-03-12 - Security review draft uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/SEC/ENG-65555-threat-model. Marcus: pending review comments around queued redact cache encryption.

2026-03-14 - Engineering: started integration tests for trace correlation across tool-call spans. Found an edge case where tool-call metadata sometimes lost on retry; added a compensating header write.
